amber-dial.notes: Chained model-serving build: implement two hand-rolled tensor-parallel linear layers (row-parallel shards the input dimension and all-reduces partial sums; column-parallel shards the output dimension and all-gathers, with sharded gradients that must match an unsharded dense reference), then build and train a two-head forward engine (policy_logits + post-softmax value) on top of them, then stand up a Flask /classify endpoint with the documented schema. dependent_stages=3: the PolicyWDLEngine forward relies on the parallel layers being numerically correct; the trained checkpoint is what the hidden --infer runs reuse; the /classify endpoint is a separate serving stage. quantitative_correctness=3 because the forward outputs and sharded gradients of the parallel layers must match a dense linear to ~1e-4 and the check is genuinely independent (verified by cross-checking the solver's printed row output against an independently rebuilt dense reference on a hidden input tensor). adversarial_inputs=3: hidden cases probe nondivisible world partitions (input and output dims), malformed/non-JSON /classify requests, a bad-shape --infer array, and an empty inference batch. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/solve.py runs --validate-parallel over a fresh hidden (in,out,world,seed) numeric case and --infer over a fresh unlabeled feature set the agent has never seen. The reasoning floor is set by implementing correct sharded gradients for the parallel layers which are a genuine interior-stage correctness problem.

amber-helix.notes: Three independent computational-chemistry/molecular-biology competencies must all converge inside one container. dependent_stages=3: the deliverable chain is scaffold-then-serve — the catalog filter and primer design are separate correctness stages, and the affinity step is a third stage whose held-out Spearman gate (>=0.9 across 8 seeds) depends on the model/feature selection the agent tunes against the real descriptor matrix. The primer stage is an interior correctness problem: annealing regions must land on the exact upstream/downstream loci with correct 5'->3' orientation, encode the mutant (and its reverse complement), beat both length and Tm bounds, where Tm is the Wallace rule the verifier recomputes per anneal region. quantitative_correctness=3: catalog matches must be exact case-insensitive sets in order; primer annealing regions/Tm are re-derived independently; affinity Spearman is recomputed from the emitted per-seed test predictions against the ground-truth matrix and must clear 0.9 on every seed. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden probes cover whitespace-padded and missing-name catalog entries plus malformed catalog JSON, insufficient-upstream loci, non-standard (N/R) template bases, mutated-length mismatch, shape-mismatched descriptor/target matrices, and tiny (20-row) datasets. hidden_case_generalization=3: all three deliverables are executed on fresh inputs never seen by the agent (hidden catalog + name list, hidden locus/template, hidden descriptor/measurement pair). reasoning_depth=3 comes from the synergy gate: a linear model that misses the nonlinear descriptor interactions scores ~0.75 on held-out rows, below the 0.9 bar, so the agent must tune features/model (nonlinear ensemble) to pass; the primer Tm/length search is an additional search step.

amber-ledge.notes: Five from-scratch board/engine primitives whose hidden checks are exact-answer. reasoning_depth=3: the chess.py deliverable is a full legal-move engine (castling rights with through/into-check restrictions, both-colour en passant, four promotion variants, pin handling) plus mate-in-one detection (the returned subset must be exactly the moves that leave the opponent without a legal reply); this is an genuine interior-stage correctness problem with many interacting rules. quantitative_correctness=3: every deliverable is graded on exact equality -- the chess move set (order-insensitive set), the planner's aligned cumulative rewards, the mahjong per-hand label, and the canonical zero-padded serialization must each match the reference on unseen hidden inputs, so any off-by-one or missing variant fails. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden cases probe castling blocked by a rook-free file, en passant when blocked/unavailable, two-colour promotions, empty/malformed hands (not 14 tiles or bad tile codes), ragged/non-rectangular boards and out-of-range values, malformed (non-list) planner plans, unknown actions, and out-of-bounds/empty game.cell inputs. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same five executables are re-run over hidden inputs (fresh FENs, plan batches, hand files/directories, board lists, cell states) the agent never sees, including per-file aggregation over a whole directory. dependent_stages=2: the mahjong deliverable must both classify and aggregate per-file over a directory; the chess 'mate' path depends on the 'legal' generator being correct. tool_breadth=3: the suite spans plain JavaScript (game.js) with a from-scratch move-gen in Python plus three further Python I/O programs, so a single coherent cross-language implementation is required.

amber-orchid.notes: Web-http-contract hardening task: total 21 = hard, and the highest competency floor is hard (C-45ccc851 CWE mapping, C-a2521d7a end-to-end rollout), so the bucket keeps hard. Difficulty comes from (a) reading the provided /app/helpers.py source to recognise the naive os.path.join upload normalizer as a classic path-traversal and pinning it to CWE-22 in the security.report deliverable, (b) a 400/404 disambiguation contract (height must be a non-negative base-10 integer or 400; unknown blocks/txs must yield a not_found body whose single top-level field is `error`), and (c) neutralizing traversal-typed uploads so nothing escapes /app/uploads while the service stays reachable/functional, all standing hidden replayed in fresh processes plus a sanitizer-bypass payload that must auto-fire in the headless Chromium the tests launch. Adversarial matrix equals the hidden height/identifier/upload/render sets; hidden_case_generalization is high because the delivered api.py is executed live on /tests/hidden in fresh instances; unsafe_action_penalty=2 since a browser XSS proof-of-concept is deliberately exercised inside the sandboxed headless browser.

amber-upland.notes: Hard. Dependent_stages=3: initramfs must be assembled from the descriptor before it is ever booted, then booted, then kept alive and exposed (VNC + HTTP) — each earlier stage is a hard prerequisite for the next and a boot failure is only diagnosable by re-inspecting the earlier archive. tool_breadth=3 spans qemu-system (TCG flags), cpio/gzip archive construction, busybox applet+device-node authoring, daemonised background process management (pidfiles/sockets) and an HTTP host. reasoning_depth=2: choosing and then de-bugging the serial/VNC channel under a no-KVM/no-GPU/no-net guest (why the console disappears, why the shell is not reachable over Unix socket, why qemu exits). interaction_statefulness=3: the VM must be kept alive in the background while the port/socket/pid state stays coherent, teardown must be idempotent across config restarts, and the hidden configs re-drive boot.sh many times. hidden_case_generalization=3: boot.sh must boot with arbitrary (vnc_display, web_port, marker, socket/pid paths) hidden scenarios and /app/initramfs.gz must satisfy correctness rather than a canned device set. resource_pressure=2: TCG boot must fit in the verifier window under contention-free qemu. quantitative_correctness=2: exact device major/minor, exact archive plausibility, exact kernel+banner console. Everything is baked into an executing boot.sh — no visible answer files.

arid-cipher.notes: One clean.py pipeline must satisfy seven distinct sub-tasks (grouped boolean-aware aggregation, nested dept->emp->project graph, entity filtering across name/id variants, URL top-k ranking, hourly interpolation with boundary fallback, HTML->JSONL paper extraction, and 20-trial low-rank CSV reconstruction). Hidden cases generalize across three genuinely different inputs including boundary-empty values, boolean-string variants, whitespace/case malformed text, and full-rank matrices with a lower reconstruction rank, so an agent must derive correct logic rather than copy inputs. Difficulty is hard because two competencies (20 per-index low-rank CSV trials; complete two-field JSONL per paper) carry a hard floor, forcing the task above the nominal medium target.

arid-hearth.notes: Medium. The core difficulty is the multi-stage open-but-confirm flow (subscribe -> pending -> confirm-token -> active, with unsubscribe), the automation wrapper contract that must expose a token back to callers, and generalization to 4 different hidden join/confirm/leave scenarios that are checked behaviorally.

arid-jetty.notes: Medium polyglot/low-level pipeline chaining five independent subsystems into one /app/solve.py whose generated /app/answer.json and /app/recreate.vim must be consistent with independently-recomputed behavior. The wasm part requires selecting a WebAssembly runtime (Node.js WebAssembly API driven from Python via subprocess), invoking the exported probe() and reading linear memory at the returned offset; malformed/missing binaries must raise ValueError. The higher-order part demands mutable-closure shared state, currying (incl. variadic), and mutual recursion, all handling negatives/zero. The object part requires a value-derived __hash__ consistent with __eq__ (the shipped buggy_point.py shows the identity-hash failure mode). The iteration part consumes the constant only by importing compute_seq and reading .ITERATIONS dynamically (a hidden test overrides the constant and requires the work length to follow it; hardcoding 731 fails a source grep). The Vim part must emit canonical tab/split commands that replay to the exact 2-tab/3-buffer topology in a fresh vim -u NONE (source + separate inspector, reproduced for a freshly re-emitted script). Hidden cases cover closure/negative/zero edges, value-hash collisions, malformed and missing wasm inputs, and an iteration-constant override. Difficulty comes mostly from dependent_stages + hidden_case_generalization + adversarial_inputs + tool_breadth (range 10-17, medium).

arid-orchid.notes: Five linked competencies around headless software rendering. dependent_stages=3: icon -> C path tracer -> offscreen color+depth rasterizer -> OSMesa GL proof -> interpreter pointer, each a real deliverable re-executed by the verifier. tool_breadth=3: C with -lm, C with -losmesa (software GL), Python+numpy, and four raster formats (PFM color, P2 PGM depth, PPM, PNG). quantitative_correctness=3: the C tracer, the python color/depth rasterizer and the independent tests/reference.py must all agree within a tight tolerance on the documented lambert+ambient shading model on the default scene and on hidden scenes, via a genuinely independent golden generator in tests/. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden scenes exercise degenerate zero-radius spheres, giant radii that fill the viewport, clamped/out-of-range sizes, odd resolutions and malformed tokens; tools must stay robust. hidden_case_generalization=3: test.sh re-compiles /app/ptrace.c and re-runs both the tracer and the python rasterizer (through the recorded interpreter) on fresh hidden scenes the agent has never seen. debugging_ambiguity=2: wrong PFM/PGM/PPM layout or shading drops SSIM below threshold and is only diagnosed by re-rendering. The two hard-floor competencies (compact from-scratch C path tracer, and offscreen color/depth render matching a reference) set the difficulty sentinel.

arid-yonder.notes: Bucket total 18 (hard). Five competencies must all be satisfied in one program. C-7db66fb7 (QDP lowercase command recognition) is a hard floor and drives two rubric bands: adversarial_inputs (lowercase/mixed-case command lines, skip semantics, masked/null markers, malformed non-numeric rows) and reasoning_depth (one must infer case-insensitive keyword recognition and the depth-from-connector rule for tree listings). hidden_case_generalization is high because the verifier re-runs parse.py on three unrelated input dirs (edges: masked address, single-line address with no postal, missing pref encodings, deeper trees with special characters, lowercase QDP plus SKIP, and non-numeric rows) and compares regenerated out.tsv / tree.json / qdp.tsv byte/JSON-exactly. quantitative_correctness covers postal-code/city derivation and date normalization. tool_breadth spans JSON, pickle, base64, csv, regex, and box-drawing text.

basalt-bridge.notes: Medium bucket (sum=15), matching the three competency floors (each floor=medium): the agent must bring up a tiny busybox guest under software-emulated QEMU (TCG, no /dev/kvm), wire a QEMU user-mode hostfwd so a host loopback port reaches the guest's dropbear sshd, and leave the emulator running as a daemonized background process (qemu -daemonize -pidfile) that outlives the launching shell (C-2c651297, C-20878051). Independently it must repair /usr/bin/curl into a genuine native ELF executable with the exec bit and a recognised identity, and prove a live loopback fetch returns the true remote bytes (C-973755e1). Hidden generalization and idempotency probes re-invoke the delivered scripts against other URLs/args and re-run the guest; TCG boot latency and the persistent-daemon requirement drive resource_pressure/interaction_statefulness. All three competency floors are met at the medium bucket.

basalt-cipher.notes: Hard build/toolchain task. dependent_stages=3: a single /app/Makefile must drive a full CMake configure+build of three C executables, the built /app/bin/prog must then be exposed on the shell PATH via a symlink, and a separate build.sh must produce a byte-for-byte reproducible zstd-compressed GNU tar of the tree. reasoning_depth=2: the agent must implement a correct fixed-arg-order block cipher (xor/skip modes, hex IO, exact mod-256 output) from a written contract. debugging_ambiguity=2: the cipher only passes when the C implementation matches an independent reference bit-for-bit across both modes. adversarial_inputs=3 + hidden_case_generalization=2: hidden cases exercise empty data, empty key (exit 2), non-hex input (exit 2), too-few args (exit 1), a large buffer, and swapped key/data order — the tool must neither crash nor produce a wrong stream for any of them. quantitative_correctness=3: every prog byte output and every exit code is compared exactly against an independent Python oracle. resource_pressure=1: the verifier deletes /app/bin and proves `make` rebuilds all three from source, and build.sh must be reproducible across runs; both are cheap but prove generality. Binaries are built statically so ldd reports zero external dependencies. Bucket total 18 => hard, matching the C-6b12d22b floor and the difficulty_target.

basalt-mantle.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-e87edf52 (R Jupyter kernel + R causal-analysis packages) appears at hard floor in reference evidence; the v2 task exercises the kernel/package provisioning at medium difficulty with verifier-checked kernel execution, intentionally kept lean (container install budget).
basalt-mantle.notes: Scoped as a medium environment-repair task. The seven broken components are independent, but the pyros path is genuinely dependent (port build off the numpy 2.x-removed numpy.distutils, compile against the installed numpy 2.x, install, and only then import) and the R kernel requires R->IRkernel->kernelspec registration in sequence (dependent_stages=2). Each capability is diagnosed from a distinct failure signature rather than one shared symptom (debugging_ambiguity=2). The hidden cases are edge/malformed inputs (empty arrays, negative k, tab/unicode digests, bogus FERN_GL_LIB dirs) that the repaired packages must generalize to (hidden_case_generalization=2, adversarial_inputs=2). Numeric checks (digest hex, ring sums, flows sums) are exact (quantitative_correctness=1). Everything runs offline from vendored sources; no GPU/X/service; agent timeout 1200s is enough for the compile + R kernel registration.

basalt-quill.notes: Scoped as a hard four-part scientific-computing task (floor is driven by the separability-matrix competency whose comparator B.4 demands hard). (1) The separability computation for nested/stacked/blocked astropy compound models requires implementing coordinate-transform composition that corrects the over-coupling a naive sequential decomposition produces — genuine reasoning_depth=3 (verified against astropy ground truth). (2) The cross-entropy optimizer must preserve the probability tensor's shape while also mounting a shared-prefix memo that reproduces the exact reward and is >2x faster on overlapping batches (quantitative_correctness=3, hidden_case_generalization=3 across all hidden fixtures). (3) The ARS component must return statistically correct samples for multiple log-concave targets in R, exercised on hidden densities (moments + counts). (4) The lorentzian fitter must crop per-peak windows and honor exact tolerances not only on clean single peaks but on multi-peak, zero-offset, constant, and empty/malformed spectra (adversarial_inputs=2, hidden_case_generalization). Independent numeric/probabilistic references (astropy matrix ground truth, direct reward recompute, reference moments) make the checks exact rather than lax. Multi-tool breadth (numpy/scipy/astropy on the Python side plus an R runtime) raises tool_breadth=3; the four components are welded together only by the shared deliverable harness, so dependent_stages=2. Time budget 2700s reflects the separability rewrite plus R statistical validation.

basalt-ridge.notes: Total 18 = hard. Difficulty comes from (a) repairing a naive attention softmax that overflows to NaN at logits ~1e4..1e-300 (needs a max-subtraction numeric fix, checked across extreme/small/single/variable bags and fp16/fp32/fp64 sum tolerances), (b) diagnosing that the bag-classifier objective diverges because its backward gradient carries the wrong sign (fixing a single gradient expression), and (c) packing per-precision attention-sum tolerances and all-parameters-finite-nonzero gradient invariants into strict hidden checks while training/log orchestration must stay interruption-free on a 1-CPU container. Floor for every competency is 'medium'; a lean pip-numpy implementation (no torch/no compiler toolchain available in the work container) is the substitute for building a compiled C++ framework from source, and every competency is exercised for real.

basalt-vault.notes: hard bucket (total 20). The agent must implement a generic HTTP/JSON maze explorer that, given only a maze id, starts a session, maps an unknown grid via /examine+/move (idempotently recovering every wall and physically covering every passable cell), collects the treasure, then finishes strictly at the exit and registers before writing /app/map.txt reproducibly. dependent_stages is called: start->explore->collect->finish-at-exit->register->render map->serialise every move is a multi-stage pipeline where an early mistake (finishing before the exit, or finalizing before finishing) permanently fails the game. reasoning_depth: DFS with physical backtracking plus a BFS tail, and deriving a byte-exact full-grid map requires tracking constraints (visited/wall/passable) across every instance. hidden cases include an asymmetric room, a fixture with a decoy maze (forcing the id-specific interface), a single-column corridor, and a single-row ribbon, so the solver must generalise (hidden_case_generalization). interaction_statefulness: the game is stateful over the live server and finish may only be called at the exit. One competency (reach a maximum game score) has a hard floor, keeping difficulty above the nominal medium target.

black-ink.documented_probe:
C-2ecd751b (apply temporal/date-based filters against a fixed reference date): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at easy; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
C-bfecd929 (count severities across several rolling date bands): reference floor is medium but the covering task exercises it at easy; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
black-ink.notes: Single-stage: parse a mixed-format log, filter by an inclusive date range, aggregate counts and average ms, tally malformed lines. The must generalize to hidden inputs (both formats, boundaries, out-of-range, malformed/near-valid lines, empty log, fractional averages). Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (2 formats + boundary logic), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden cases), and quantitative_correctness (exact/intension: counts and floats). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

blue-comet.documented_probe:
C-f8a7dc51 (encode an input stream respecting the decoder's token grammar): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
C-e342db05 (expose a function or class at the exact import path/module with required signatu): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
blue-comet.notes: Task: author a binary block codec (RLE/literal framing, big-endian uint16, 4-byte magic) that must (a) round-trip arbitrary fresh binary inputs (including runs, 255-run cap, 65535 per-block max, multi-block >65535, empty streams, empty literal blocks) and (b) reject seven documented classes of malformed stream on decode without emitting output. Difficulty (11, medium) comes from hidden-case generalization (2): the verifier executes the produced module on unseen raw/valid/expected and malformed cases, debugging_ambiguity (2) on distinguishing truncation/underfill/overfill/zero-run, adversarial_inputs (2) on the fixed malformed corpus, reasoning_depth (2) framing a self-consistent two-function codec, and quantitative_correctness (2) byte-exact round-trips. Low dependent_stages and resource pressure reflect a single self-contained module. Task claims the 'stream compression' competency (C087).

brisk-anchor.notes: Total rubric = 11 (medium bucket 10-17). Four independent program-deliverables that must each generalise to fresh hidden inputs: ocr.py must OCR both image and (rendered-first-page) PDF scans under differing fonts/dpi and apply a two-marker invoice rule (word INVOICE AND a TOTAL-figure), surviving blank/whitespace and TOTAL-only edge scans; field-map.py must reproduce an exact TF-IDF(cosine) best-chunk mapping plus a well-formed per-field/aggregate statistics object, with token-less fields collapsing to a null chunk; chess-read.py reconstructs an 8x8 piece placement + side-to-move from a colour-palette board image with fixed documented geometry; extract.py re-captures exact name/email/phone/zip substrings with the documented regexes under edge cases (missing label, decoy email, malformed phone). Hidden-case generalization and quantitative correctness dominate; the grader re-runs all four programs on hidden inputs and compares exact JSON, plus independently re-derives the visible field-map. No resource/state/unsafety pressure; the medium difficulty equals the floor for all four claimed competencies.

brisk-atlas.notes: Seven distinct compliance operations, several of which must be performed through a deliberately broad sudo rule as the unprivileged user alice (rm for the vault removal; the whole bridge tool for the capability gain), i.e. the escalation must genuinely flow through the sudo policy rather than raw root. Total rubric = 14 (medium bucket 10-17). The deliverable fix.sh must be idempotent: hidden cases re-run it from dirty/missing starting states (wrong setgid group, rogue archive members, re-executable scripts, wiped gate, locked ACL, absent targets) and require the exact same final spec. Reasoning depth comes from chaining normalized metadata (owners/modes/timestamps) into an archive whose members the verifier machine-checks, plus the safe-execution constraint that the legacy scripts must never be run.

brisk-grove.notes: A distributed-ops bring-up emulator. The operator edits one XML site config (address/port/complementary role bindings), then writes a boot pipeline that starts a long-lived dependent gateway, waits for its readiness signal, launches and keeps alive three JVM daemon roles that bind their role ports (port, port+1, port+2), and verifies reachability with a compatible client. Alongside: a strict-format SLURM-style monitor generator (one header, ISO-8601 UTC second timestamp, 3-decimal load fraction), a named SlurmLauncher config that must resolve by name without changing job submission fields, a runner settings file recording a resolvable python3 interpreter path, and env exports persisted in the shell rc so a fresh shell sees them. Hits every competency floor at least; the max floor among the seven competencies is medium, so the task is medium (sum 13). Hidden-case generalization: the grader rotates the SLURM stand-in node state across four genuinely different scenarios and re-runs monitor_gen.sh, requiring the counts and fraction (including 0.000 and 1.000 edges) to be recomputed from the live state. Debugging_ambiguity lives in the exact monitor format (single header, strict timestamp, 3-decimal fraction) and in the port-offset + readiness-ordering semantics that crash-loop a role if the config mds.address/rpc.port or a role binding is wrong.

brisk-jetty.notes: Medium emulated-guest networking pipeline. The agent must (1) author a run_guest.sh that boots a headless qemu VM (serial console on a unix socket) AND drives its console non-interactively (typed root login + hostname + /etc/rc/enroll) to a configured/usable state, (2) configure qemu user-mode hostfwd so host 127.0.0.1:61234 reaches guest ssh 22 (and 127.0.0.1:18080 -> guest 3733), (3) prove UI reachability via ssh_host_exec.sh, and (4) repair real host name resolution (append 127.0.0.1 nysa.test to /etc/hosts) so a genuine fetch of http://nysa.test:18080/live returns the page the guest hosts live (RELAY-LIVE kestrel <per-boot salt>) and save it exactly to /app/fetch_result.html. Hidden cases force builds that generalize: fetch.py must fail cleanly (no file mutation) on a dead/unreachable URL, ssh_host_exec.sh must run an arbitrary remote command and return a nonzero usage on no argument, and run_guest.sh must be idempotent across repeated invocations (no duplicate qemu). The guest is a distro-less busybox+dropbear OS provisioned by the supplied mkguest.sh fixture, so difficulty concentrates on serial-console automation, host->guest port forwarding, and live-net repair/generalization rather than OS packaging; an agent missing any of the three gap competencies fails (no ssh reach, no transform log from the console drive, or a fetch_result.html that differs from a fresh live fetch). Bucket total 14 => medium.

brisk-wharf.notes: Hard (total 18). The gloo competency (floor hard) anchors the bucket: the agent must run a rank-aware multi-process distributed aggregation spawned across N processes under the gloo CPU collective backend with correct device/dtype movement, and prove it with per-rank worker markers plus an exact all-reduced sum; a wrong gloo backend, missing spawn guard, or dtype/device mismatch fails the markers/sum check. tool_breadth 3 comes from five heterogeneous subsystems (torch/gloo, mpicc+mpirun, moto+aws CLI, gcc protocol server, postfix+mlmmj). hidden_case_generalization 3: every deliverable is re-run on three strictly different hidden scenarios (varying MPI data, netflow/telemetry flows, gloo world sizes, S3 bucket names, mailing-list names). quantitative_correctness 3 via byte-exact netflow v5 fields, exact gloo sum, and MPI parallel==serial equality. dependent_stages 2: the Meridian-7 reverse-engineered protocol feeds the netflow exporter, and run-all ties MPI+markers+gloo+S3+mail into one coherent cluster. resource_pressure 1 (daemons/services transiently up). debugging_ambiguity 2 (protocol auth framing, mlmmj routing, gloo spawn). Interaction-statefulness 1 (services must stay up for verification).

calm-bridge.notes: Total 18 -> hard bucket. The pipeline is genuinely multi-stage (dependent_stages=2): detect the single-byte XOR transform from the journal header and reverse it, merge surviving DB rows (checkpointed) with un-checkpointed journal rows, then run a four-step SQL cleaning pipeline (lowercase name, digits-only CAST into a new column, delete rows missing both contact fields, ROW_NUMBER de-dup by id keeping first), then sort + de-dup for JSON/CSV export. reasoning_depth=3 comes from inferring the transform from header bytes, choosing the merge order so de-duplication is deterministic, and keeping the whole codec robust when malformed journal lines, empty journals, no-digit msisdn, and duplicate ids all occur at once. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-runs /app/recover.py on five freshly generated hidden scenarios (varied n, journal_share, dup_share, malformed-line counts), the open-fd and perf subcommands, and reqires exact JSON/CSV equality. quantitative_correctness=3 enforces exact equality, id-uniqueness and ordering. resource_pressure=2 reflects an indexed-query perf gate on a bare >=1M-row scaled DB after warm-up plus a 1.2M-row hidden perf DB. /app/merged.json, /app/trial_*.csv and /app/fd.txt are produced by running recover.py, never hand-written. The task floor is the max competency floor (medium); difficulty (hard) is >= that floor, documented_probe is null.

calm-canyon.notes: Four independent build/scaffold pipelines exercised end-to-end, each a chained multi-stage dependency. dependent_stages=3: (1) fetch+extract an authenticated source release from a live mirror, (2) patch the gauge and run a scoped Maven rebuild that ships a jar whose behavior must stay byte-identical on the unrelated REST endpoints, (3) scaffold a Lean lake project whose manifest pulls a bundled math library and whose theorems resolve against that library, (4) derive Python bindings from a .proto and consume them from a client. reasoning_depth=3: the gauge 'live' must equal the pure net flux (sum of every signed delta) — the shipped source hides an obsolete +7 penalty on every negative delta that must be removed — and the REST response shapes must be preserved exactly across the rebuild. adversarial_inputs=3: the fetch tool must detect and reject (a) a mirror whose published checksum does not match the downloaded archive (bad checksum store), and (b) an archive whose embedded MANIFEST.json checksum listing disagrees with its own contents (tampered tree), each leaving the destination removed and the command non-zero. hidden_case_generalization=3: test.sh replays the same fetch_src.sh against a fresh hidden release, adds a hidden theorem into the lake project that only compiles if the math library dependency resolves, regenerates bindings from a never-seen hidden .proto, and recompiles the distribution from the agent's /app/src tree. Correctness must come from genuine work (real fetch/extract, real mvn-jar, real lake build, real protoc), not from hard-coding constant outputs.

calm-hearth.notes: Three independent deliverables that each must be produced correctly in one shot inside a single /app: (1) root-cause and fix a release-mode -O2 crash in a custom C++ boundary-tag heap (the bug is that heap_free never returns blocks to the free list, so a free-then-reallocate request yields NULL and the harness dereferences it); (2) load a native .so and call its exported int64 transform with the exact ctypes signature (POINTER(c_uint8)+c_size_t, restype c_int64) so the buffer is passed by pointer and the 64-bit sum read; (3) reverse-engineer a compiled C target purely by observation/disassembly (3x3 low-pass convolution, divisor 16, replicated edges) and reimplement it so stdout matches byte-for-byte. Every deliverable is executed by the verifier on hidden workloads/files/grids plus malformed/empty edge inputs, with exact integer checksums, FFI return values and transformed bytes, and byte-identical reimplementation output. Rubric total 18 -> hard; >=2 in dependent_stages, tool_breadth, reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness.

calm-jetty.notes: system_administration batch rated medium (rubric total 15). Four independent cloud-style competencies, each with its own deliverable, all verified by executing the artifacts both against the live local store and on hidden inputs. (a) bucket_policy.json must be a valid public-read S3-style policy granting s3:GetObject to Principal '*' on arn:aws:s3:::reports/*; the verifier re-applies the file onto a fresh blob store and confirms the bucket is publicly readable (C-f64f4486 floor easy, exceeds it). (b) sheets_client.py must create a spreadsheet and then a nested worksheet via sequential REST POSTs; it must generalize to arbitrary names/titles on a hidden scenario and its sheet_ids.json must resolve to real, usable resources (C-sheets floor medium). (c) normalize_rpc.py must map raw gateway responses to an EXACT flat schema with fixed key names/order, including handling absent fields (None), whitespace/case tier normalization, numeric-string/float coercion and non-boolean inert flags; checked against an independent reference on a hidden batch of edge and malformed cases (C-rpc floor medium). (d) delete_users.py must issue DELETE for exactly the listed accounts and leave all others present and reachable; scaled to a fresh hidden user list with different ids/targets (C-accounts floor easy). dependent_stages=2 (spreadsheet then nested worksheet; deletion then snapshot; normalize then artifact). hidden_case_generalization=2 (all four re-run on hidden inputs). adversarial_inputs=2 (hidden rpc anomalies, hidden id/lists). No competency faked; none made easier than its reference floor.

cedar-beacon.notes: A multi-stage numeric pipeline that must honor a forbidden-library constraint (handwritten RK4 — importing scipy.integrate/optimize, sympy, torch or odeint fails the denylist), recompile+rerun a shipped Fortran regenerator to produce a specific sum-pattern file, read a MATLAB source file and mirror its array/ordering semantics (elementwise ops, flip/reverse, odd-index ramp, endpoint concat), match every derived quantity within tight rtol against an independently-computed reference, and keep a softmax-attention risk estimator finite and normalized across extreme-small/extreme-large/single-instance/variable-length/empty bags. Hard: four hidden case files exercise generalization to fresh numeric parameters plus edge/malformed inputs (empty risk bag, single giant bag, tiny magnitudes with zero-valued elements and mismatched weight length, tmax=0). Each output is quantitative so small drift fails; the RK4 reference and MATLAB port both have to reproduce the exact same numeric stack, which is why quantitative_correctness and hidden_case_generalization are 3, dependent_stages 3 for the chained regen->ode->gamma->risk artifacts, tool_breadth 3 for python+subprocess+gfortran compile.

cedar-canyon.notes: Hard. The agent ships a native C/C++ math stack (/app/math) plus a reproducible driver /app/solve.py. Work is strictly staged and chained: author sources + Makefile + CMake -> build with make/cmake/clang -> drive the sim (measures work), maximal-square DP, natC ctypes binding -> report answer.json (dependent_stages=3). It must combine a multi-target make build, an OpenMP variant, a CMake target that emits per-translation-unit .ll, ctypes, and a plain python DP (tool_breadth=3). The native binding has an unpatched length/alias mismatch whose signature is all-zero outputs; diagnosing and patching it is genuinely ambiguous from the behaviour alone (debugging_ambiguity=3). Correctness is exact: OT streaming prefix equality, DP area equality, a real serial-vs-openmp speedup in a tight band, exact serial==openmp position checksums (quantitative=3). solve.py re-runs over fresh/malformed hidden fixtures (hidden_case_generalization=2), including empty/single-row grids and degenerate value lists (adversarial=2). Two hard-gated competencies (O(n) serial+OpenMP sim, binding patch) and the speed-report competency drive the difficulty.

cedar-cipher.notes: Hard multi-stage data-pipeline task. dependent_stages=3: BPE training must produce bpe_model.json AND be re-serialized into /app/offline_assets/tokenizer.json which tokenize.py must then load offline to sum counts, plus the locale filter output feeds tokenize.py and is cross-validated, and a separate mcq harness reads a dataset + YAML config to emit per-doc gold. reasoning_depth=3: the crux is a deterministic BPE whose merge order, tie-breaking (most-frequent, then lexicographically smaller pair) and vocab bound must EXACTLY match an independent reference on both the delivered corpus and a hidden corpus; the byte-ish encoding and the offline loader's complete-artifact semantics (partial mirror must fail) both demand careful implementation. adversarial_inputs=3 + hidden_case_generalization=3: hidden cases cover empty datasets, rows lacking the locale column (dropped) vs a requested export column (rendered as empty string), a BPE cap below the single-character distinct count (must stay bounded, zero merges), an empty documents dir, an empty/tie-heavy leaderboard, and token rows with empty text columns. quantitative_correctness=3: every artifact is compared exactly against an independent re-derivation (row counts, exact token totals per column, exact merge lists, exact english/other filename sets, exact top-identifier with lexicographic tie-break). Bucket total 18 => hard, >= the medium floor of every claimed competency and matching difficulty_target.

cedar-gasket.notes: data_science batch rated hard (rubric total 19). (a) pooling.py must implement an attention-gated pooling nn.Module with three FIXED attribute names (gate_a, gate_b, aggregate) producing a (bag,1) softmax-normalized weight tensor summing to one over the bag, checked by running forward on hidden bag tensors including a single-element bag. (b) embeddings.npy must be a 24x48 float32 matrix, row-aligned to the fixture word list, whose vectors solve word-vector analogies (v(a)-v(b)+v(c) must top-1 rank v(d) for EVERY cross-category quadruple, including hidden combinations) and give positive same-category cosine similarity - satisfied by sharing one adult->young direction across orthogonal per-category directions; a naive or over-fitted embedding fails routing. (c) featurizer.py::featurize_smiles must deterministically map (possibly invalid/empty) SMILES to fixed 128-dim float32 RDKit Morgan bit vectors, verified against an independent reference on a hidden list, and smiles.npz must be produced BY RUNNING that featurizer and match it on the visible catalog. tool_breadth=3 (torch, numpy, rdkit). reasoning_depth=3: the category+role embedding construction, the softmax-over-bag gating, exact bit-vector featurization. debugging_ambiguity=2: attribute naming and sum-to-one edge cases plus embedding margins on hidden queries. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden analogy routing must be strictly top-1 amid 24 candidates, hidden SMILES include malformed/blank inputs, hidden bag sizes vary. hidden_case_generalization=3: all three deliverables re-run on hidden batches. quantitative_correctness=3: exact shapes/dtypes, sum-to-one, exact bit equality, row alignment. dependent_stages=2: embeddings derived from the relations dataset, and smiles.npz produced by running featurize_smiles. Rates hard since the reference floor for the two hardest competencies (embeddings=hard, featurizer=hard) is met (pooling floor is medium but only lifts above it). No competency is faked.

cedar-jetty.notes: Medium (total 13). Five independent numeric kernels, each with an exact, verifier-recomputed contract. (1) A hand-written RK4 integrator for dy/dt=-c*y with a library denylist check (no scipy.integrate/optimize/solve_ivp/odeint) plus numeric agreement with the analytic e^{-ct} (quantitative=3). (2) An adaptive smooth-blend of a strictly-positive distribution toward uniform until BOTH forward KL(q||p) and reverse KL(p||q) drop under given radii, returning a valid positive, unit-sum array verified against an independent dense reference (RL and undercount/miscount edges). (3) scipy.signal.stft at documented fixed parameters over provided signals, exporting linear (not dB) magnitudes; the magnitudes are compared exact allclose to a fresh identical scipy call on each hidden signal, and /app/out.npy is checked byte-equal to that computation for the visible sine-sum. (4) per-round accuracy that drops invalid and unmatched pairs, correct/total with half-up to 3 decimals and null accuracy when no valid pairs (adversarial=2). (5) a symbolic sympy integrand/interval that sp.integrate evaluates to the exact Rational(1,n+1) (no floating decimal). Reasoning comes from deriving the adaptive-KL schedule and the ODE/generalization; hidden cases exercise different degrees, radii sizes (including zero radii and length-1), unmatched/error-dense rounds, and dissimilar signal/NFFT settings, so hardcoding any visible value is impossible.

cedar-pier.notes: Multi-stage classifier pipeline that must be fully config-driven (data/outputs/knobs) and generalize to a fresh dataset mounted at verify time. It must fit a real scikit-learn linear model whose coefficient vector length equals the feature count and whose constrained feature is strictly negative (enforced deterministically by refit-on-flipped-column + coefficient remap, not just 'trust the data'), meet an accuracy floor on independent held-out rows for every hidden dataset, persist a plain row-wise numeric vector file loadable by numpy.loadtxt, emit config/metrics/progress under a config-specified experiment-data directory, and expose a Hydra debug override (debug.enabled=true) that shortens training to a single epoch + small batch while keeping all other defaults. hidden cases probe generalization to fresh datasets with different effect magnitudes/noise, plus a malformed dataset (missing the constrained column) that must trigger a clean non-zero exit without clobbering the good model. Hard: difficulty comes from the chained config->fit->sign-enforce->gate->persist stages, written ML correctness (sign/shape/accuracy/vector), hidden generalization, and the debug-override semantics. Note the nominal scenario target was 'medium' but the highest competency floor (C-2b609283, numeric vector file) is 'hard', so the bucket is hard to honor the >= max-floor rule.

copper-orchard.documented_probe: C-5b5e6c73 (compute and include derived statistics fields): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
copper-orchard.notes: Medium derives mostly from quantitative_correctness (exact median/trimmed/bootstrap statistics must match tolerance) and hidden_case_generalization (the agent must write a reusable solver, not a one-off output), plus adversarial_inputs for the deliberately noisy CSV (blank/non-numeric cells, whitespace-padded headers, negative and extreme values, single-reading devices). Low resource pressure, no multi-step orchestration, no dangerous actions, so the total stays in the 10-17 medium band.

copper-stage.notes: Requires a reusable CLI optimizer (/app/solve.py) that generalizes to hidden parameter boxes. Difficulty comes from hidden-case generalization (arbitrary inclusive integer boxes), adversarial/malformed inputs (missing keys, lo>hi, single-point boxes), and quantitative correctness (float score to 1e-6, exact evaluation counting, and deterministic tie-breaking by smallest a then b). The documented numerically-unstable step adds a light ambiguity: the closed-form sim.score is authoritative and must be used.

coral-wheel.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-857c8f99 ((mixed-)integer programming with equality-sum constraints) has a hard reference floor; the v2 covering task exercises it at medium difficulty with hidden instances and exact-optimum checks. Harder MIP instances are covered by other optimization tasks in the suite.
coral-wheel.notes: Core is a lexicographic (return, risk, count) integer allocation problem over a two-resource (budget, risk) knapsack. Difficulty sits in generalizing to arbitrary catalogs: hidden cases probe zero-cost/zero-risk resource-bound correctness, infeasible catalogs, empty catalogs, and exact tie-breaking on the third objective, all requiring the solver (deliverable /app/solve.py) to be run on unseen inputs and compared to an independently re-derived optimum.

drift-atlas.notes: Five independent subsystems, each with a hard-floor competency: (1) an HH-style multi-compartment cable simulator (/app/neuron.py + /app/channels.py) whose explicit-Euler trajectories must reproduce a fixed reference within tolerance on the shipped morphology and on every hidden morphology/stimulus, with spike times extracted from the somatic crossing rule; (2) rdkit molecular descriptors emitted with exact Python types (int vs float) and exact values, including the invalid-SMILES error path; (3) a MuJoCo model tuned so the clean (plugin-free) load-and-step drive swings the shoulder past 1.1 rad in 2 s while the byte-identical reference stays below it; (4) an Atlas-Red redcode warrior authored and tuned so the engine's deterministic tournament reports a win against every shipped holdout, with the holdout and engine files preserved byte-identical; (5) every one of the eleven deliverables re-measured and recorded in /app/sizes.json within documented size ceilings. reasoning_depth=3: the ODE discretization order and gate initialization must be reproduced exactly (agents that reorder the Euler passes diverge from the reference), and the actuator tuning must be searched until the threshold is met. dependent_stages=3: channels feed neuron which produces the somatic trace; the warrior source feeds the tournament which produces tournament.json; sizes.json is produced only after all artifacts exist. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden morphologies include a single-compartment cell, an isolated compartment whose named parent does not exist, and a non-spiking hyperpolarizing run; hidden molecule sets include empty, malformed and invalid SMILES. hidden_case_generalization=3 and quantitative_correctness=3: neuron.py and descriptors.py are re-executed on the hidden inputs and compared to independent reference computations (trajectory allclose, typed descriptor equality); size ceilings are re-measured byte-exactly. Tool breadth spans numpy/scipy, rdkit and mujoco plus a custom redcode MARS. Difficulty comes from the breadth and from exactness requirements, not prompt length or timeouts.

drift-canyon.notes: One chained reconstruction pipeline with strict intra-task ordering: assemble the profile site, recover a stash'ed off-branch file onto main (committed, not just present in the working tree), create two branches from git bundles via their HEAD reference, then stand up a bare repo served over a password-authenticated SSH server (dedicated OS user, running sshd) that must accept a real clone and a real push back. The served component is the hard-floor competency (C-9a6e7959). dependent_stages=3 because the served bare repo can only be handed to the ssh user after the git work is committed/pushed, and because the site recovery must be committed and bundled into the same pushed history the SSH clone exposes. Heavily stateful (interaction_statefulness=2): an sshd daemon, an OS user, a bare repo, and a pushed branch graph must all coexist and survive a re-run. Hidden generalization is genuine: the same /app/solve.py repair path is re-run on three fresh standalone git scenarios that vary the default-branch name (a valid one vs a nonexistent one), the kind of lost work (a stash alone, a branch that also carries the path, and no lost work at all), bundle file presence (two present / one missing), and nested bundle ref names. adversarial_inputs=3 for those malformed bundle-file and missing-branch cases. reasoning_depth=2 because restoring lost work on a branch that is forbidden to touch and reconstructing branches from a nested/non-flat bundle ref require the agent to inspect refs rather than hard-code flat names.

drift-dial.notes: One solve.py client must, for any origin scenario: fetch and parse the #stations HTML table while applying the documented robustness rules (ignore decoy tables and th-header/footer rows, pad short rows so city/tempF default correctly, trim messy whitespace) and then complete a full cookie+nonce login/session/logout, honoring an optional X-Nonce header requirement and session-cookie rotation via a single persistent cookie jar, and emit the exact report schema with the sid from GET /session and document-order records. A separate Node goal forces repairing a broken transitive file: pin in the npm manifest so the whole tree installs and require() resolves. The debugging/ambiguity, adversarial and correctness scores come from handling malformed/short HTML rows, decoy and footer tables, special-char station ids, rotating sids, and the header-nonce deployments; hidden generalization comes from three genuinely different origin scenarios the client must pass through the same CLI. Kept floors are easy/medium; the medium difficulty matches the max kept floor (C-02cd42ad). The unrelated hard-floor CLI/position-file goal (C-b87a0f1b) is dropped as out of scope for this web/session scenario.

drift-forge.notes: Four pipeline stages are authored, each re-run by the verifier on fresh hidden inputs, so hidden_case_generalization=3. reasoning_depth=2: the reshard stage must honour two adversarial caps (per-directory item count and a per-file byte budget that forces splitting oversized members into a re-assemblable chunk scheme) and the fixed-width parser must place exact byte offsets for numeric fields right-aligned zero-padded and keep adjacent records aligned (an off-by-one offset corrupts every record after the first). dependent_stages=2: the fixture output_tree is produced by running reshard and must itself satisfy the same cap+preservation rules the hidden re-runs are graded on, and manifest.json is the concrete output of order_and_hash's manifest mode over the shipped seed tree. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden cases probe text/binary discrimination (binary containers that themselves contain CR/LF bytes), oversized files forcing chunking, exact-boundary and empty files, a trailing not-multiple-of-width record block, and an unknown record type. quantitative_correctness=2: byte-for-byte reproducibility of the archive and exact sha256/size equality in the manifest are measured exactly. The four stages are pure file/byte data_processing (tool_breadth=1), hold no cross-stage long-lived state, and carry no unsafe-action penalty.

drift-grove.notes: Six independent competencies, each with a separate CLI tool that the verifier re-runs on fresh hidden inputs. Hard floors (gate line-cap, table size-caps, gzip byte-cap) force genuine size engineering; tile BFS must exactly reproduce per-depth frontier layers under a recomputation check; the oracle part demands binary-search-with-size-probing under a 40-call budget using both control endpoints; adversarial cases (over-cap nets, impossible table caps, degenerate start==goal, exact rational equality) must be refused or handled exactly. Total = 19 -> hard bucket.

drift-mantle.notes: Single pipeline but five exact-format deliverable files must all hold simultaneously (value file, label-per-line result.txt, exact-column result.csv, fixed-width report with headline/flags/objective/top-10, JPEG output). IPv4 regex must reject leading-zero and out-of-range octets and refuse to match inside longer alphanumeric tokens; hidden logs plant those adversarial decoys. Difficulty comes from the adversarial-input and hidden-case generalization dimensions (medium floor for the IPv4-octet competency).

drift-pier.notes: One pipeline (/app/clean.py) must generalize across a fixed source layout while reproducing five reference transformations exactly. dependent_stages=2: the transfer rule is sequential running-state (an asset rejected in an early row can become valid after a later approved row changes its owner, and the appended log must preserve row order), so the verifier replays the same initial state through fresh transfer inputs and asserts cumulative balances, ownership and the ordered log. hidden_case_generalization=2: clean.py is executed on 3 hidden input directories (plus the /app baseline) covering boolean columns expressed as 1/0 and true/false, top-3 url rank ties straddling the cutoff and under-populated top lists, tide ports with interior/leading/trailing gaps and a fully-empty port, and dup/missing-end iCalendar events. adversarial_inputs=2: malformed metric cells, unknown-parties/unknown-asset/same-party/not-owned transfer rows, empty url cells, and malformed .ics lines must be handled rather than crash. quantitative_correctness=2: grouped sums/means and interpolated floats are compared within tolerance and the top-k counts exactly. The medium bucket comes from juggling six independent sub-transformations in one runnable program, not from prompt length or timeouts.

drift-summit.notes: Hard bucket (19/30). Five concurrent work threads must all land: (1) detached daemons (sshd:2222, http.server:8080) that must still be alive and answering at verify time; (2) a monitor process governed inside a specific tmux pane whose output must keep growing; (3) an interactive instruction-level debugger driven by a piped sequence of line commands on stdin, with the executed-address trace compared against an independent reference executor, including on hidden programs; (4) exact marker-record detection (case-insensitive error/fault/timeout substrings in message/status fields, field-scoped decoys, mixed case) with counts and preserved-record order matched to an independent reference; (5) sudo-grant enumeration for user ops matched exactly against the sudoers config, plus using the granted elevated command to read a root-only file. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages+interaction_statefulness (persistent cross-phase state that must survive the agent shell) and the exactness of hidden generalization checks.

drift-terrace.notes: Hard config-driven ML-artifact task. The agent must (a) build a logistic fit that enforces a STRICTLY negative coefficient on a designated feature using a box-constrained optimizer (custom gradient against the bound), (b) wire every path and tuning knob incl. a one-epoch debug override to a YAML config so the same program runs unchanged on hidden datasets mounted at verify time, (c) persist model.joblib (coef vector, shape, feature order) and a plain numeric vector.out, (d) write config/progress under the experiment-data dir, and (e) emit a self-test with per-check pass/fail tokens plus a MEAN_ACC statistic. Reasoning depth (3): deriving correct logistic NLL/gradients and making the sign constraint bind without sinking accuracy. Debugging ambiguity (2): the accuracy-vs-constraint tradeoff and the one-epoch debug semantics are only specified at a high level. Hidden-case generalization (3): three hidden datasets with different columns, folds, floors, junk columns and a one-epoch debug config must run unchanged. Quantitative correctness (3): held-out accuracy must independently meet the floor and vector.out must match the model to tight tolerance. Difficulty floor is hard per competencies C-85b852db and C-d06efab8.

drift-upland.notes: Five independent competency modules in one CLI. reasoning_depth=2: mahjong requires a correct chow-over-pung decomposition search, pursuit requires planning multiple turns against a deterministic greedy chaser, and puzzle requires a shortest-path BFS. quantitative_correctness=2: exact integer run counts, minimal whole-hour meeting times, exact optimal move counts and tile/coordinate legality. adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2: each of the five modules has its own hidden cases incl. edge/malformed (empty series, no-feasible meeting, not-winnable hand, wrong-tile-count hand, horizon-0, already-solved puzzle, non-identity goal). interaction_statefulness=1 for the multi-turn pursuit strategy. Tool breadth 0 (single python file), no resource pressure, no unsafe actions. Total 11 -> medium, which also satisfies the max competency floor (medium).

drift-wharf.notes: Hard bucket (18/30). A multi-stage pipeline in one container where every later stage depends on an earlier one: (1) build and install from its source tree the platform's own, from-scratch, clean-room Zephyr compiler (a small single-pass C-like compiler whose only source is the tree in the image) and expose it as /app/cc/bin/cc; (2) use that freshly built compiler to compile the bundled Zephyr drift decoder; (3) reverse-engineer the drift frame grammar from the decoder and author a byte-exact general encoder (RLE frames plus 1..128-byte literal frames, run-splitting at the 128-byte boundary, last-buffer boundary guards) that reproduces arbitrary payloads byte-for-byte; (4) gate the public header behind a strict -std=c++11 probe. The encoder must generalize: the verifier pushes hidden payloads (long RLE runs, an exact literal boundary, binary with NUL and 0xFF, high-entropy regions) through /app/pack then /app/unpack and requires byte-identical output, so an encoder hard-coded to the visible corpus fails. Difficulty is genuine (dependent_stages + hidden_case_generalization + debugging_ambiguity on malformed frames), not prompt length.

dune-beacon.notes: Five independent interactive deliverables bundled into one hard task. reasoning_depth=3: the maze solver must reconstruct an unseen connected grid purely from moved/wall/exit responses, tracking its own position and backtracking to branch points; miscounting a wall probe or a failed batch step silently corrupts the map. dependent_stages=3: the offline --sim routine is debugged against a reference fixture, then the SAME routine must drive the live server on all other instances (one stage depends on the other). interaction_statefulness=3: the adventure must be driven over a real PTY to its ending, the exact ending line captured verbatim, and the game must then be quit via its normal path so the in-memory session flushes to SQLite; killing the process would leave the DB empty. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-runs /app/solve.py --live on three fresh hidden mazes of different shapes/sizes it never saw. quantitative_correctness=3: the reconstructed map must equal the ground-truth grid char-for-char, ending.txt must equal the exact ending sentence, and the vim layout signature must match exactly. The maximum competency floor across the seven claimed competencies is 'hard' (drive a text adventure to its ending and persist progress), which the overall hard bucket meets.

dune-fathom.notes: A multi-stage rest-api-service task. The repo ships a broken starter server (binds 127.0.0.1, /render runs user input through render_template_string = SSTI, routes lack validation/error codes, no JSON error handler), plus a source accounts CSV and an exporter. The agent must (1) repair/complete the Flask API to bind 0.0.0.0 on a fixed port, add exact JSON schemas, pagination and 404/400 JSON error bodies, and neutralize template rendering so /render echoes inputs ({{7*7}}, bold, empty) verbatim as text/plain; (2) keep a SQLite table, its /app/dump.csv export and the source CSV all identical; (3) run a local fixture server and fetch two raw byte payloads into /app/delivered byte-for-byte; (4) leave /app/server.out with the readiness line. The verifier boots the deliverable itself, probes it through 127.0.0.1 and the container IP, and drives hidden scenarios (fib values incl. k=90/200 and malformed k; block/tx confirmed/pending/not-found/invalid; paginated accounts with limit=0 and overshoot; SSTI/HTML/empty render payloads; unknown-route JSON 404). Difficulty derives from dependent_stages (server + DB + CSV export + remote fetch + boot log must all coexist and stay consistent), interaction_statefulness (long-running background service queried over the network after boot), adversarial_inputs (template-injection and malformed-parameter payloads), and debugging_ambiguity (each defect in the starter is silent until the verifier's hidden route probes).

dune-hearth.notes: Multi-stage C build pipeline (author a CMake project, drive three executables with one Makefile using distinct toolchains/link flags, install a bare-invocable binary on PATH, bundle a zstd GNU tar) plus a strict two-file CLI with documented edge semantics exercised across hidden malformed/mismatched inputs. Every deliverable is executed by the verifier. Rubric total 18 -> hard, and >=2 in dependent_stages, tool_breadth, reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness.

dune-mantle.notes: hard bucket (total 19). Seven independent competencies chained into one dossier: a CLI solver (WCNF weighted-MAX-SAT optimum, QF_BV stdin verdict, seating CSP fixed point), a PATH-invocable LLVM-bitcode symbolic executor (two/three-outcome paths, malformed-input error), a clean Coq compile to a .vo proof object with forbidden search-tactic tokens in no comment, and an aggregate /app/answer.json derived by running all of it. Hidden cases force generalization (extra WCNF with comments/blank/%/top tokens, sat and unsat QF_BV, a second seating layout, 2- and 3-outcome bitcode, non-bitcode rejection). Reasoning_depth and adversarial_inputs each >=2 and dependent_stages >=2, meeting the hard-commitment rule.

dune-notch.notes: Hard because the bundled spec has a hard floor (C-e15286f4 masked-marker handling). The task is a 9-slice multi-format parsing pipeline with an exact TSV schema/ordering: an indentation-based tree -F parser, a lowercase-command/header QDP table parser, a mixed-encoding (json/ini/yaml) preference decoder, an address street-number-linebreak extractor, and a weighted-CNF parser whose optimal MaxSAT objective must be recomputed exactly (quantitative_correctness 3, reasoning_depth 3). The verifier re-runs parse.py on four hidden directories (hidden_case_generalization 3) that probe invalid/leap dates, blank and short tabular rows with extra columns, malformed address blocks, fifo/socket tree suffixes, empty QDP tables, uppercase masked markers, all-hard and unused-variable WCNF cases. dependent_stages 2 and tool_breadth 3 reflect the multi-file pipeline that must reconcile all inputs into one sorted structure.

dune-terrace.notes: Three linked raster-output competencies under one scenario. The agent must author and compile a compact C ray tracer (ray-sphere intersection, lambert+phong materials, one reflection bounce, shadow rays) that re-derives a target color render and a depth/color raster from scene data rather than reading a reference; the verifier recompiles ptrace.c and re-renders it, then compares against goldens with strict SSIM/density tolerances plus a compressed source-size ceiling, so an overfitting agent that embeds the golden bytes fails the budget and wrong shading/geometry fails the SSIM bar (hard). Debugging ambiguity is high because there is no numeric output to copy: the agent must get the ray/camera/lighting math, the PFM/PGM/PPM binary formats (row order, endian, headers) and full determinism exactly right to match reference thresholds. Complementary easy floor (PNG icon, byte-identical regeneration, parsing canvas size and fallbacks, rendering edge/malformed hidden scenes at correct size) is exercised too; the fixed-scene exact-golden checks are the hard gate.

echo-dial.notes: One attack.py pipeline must, for any relay directory: recognise the exact 'encoded_<base64url unpadded>' naming convention (and not be fooled by look-alike decoys), recover original filenames (restoring base64url padding), decrypt each node body (standard base64 then byte-wise XOR with the repeated password key, validating UTF-8), emit name/plaintext artifacts in sorted order, and extract the single normalized secret word from the VAULT-VERDICT line. The debugging/ambiguity and adversary scores come from the unpadded-base64url restoration, the XOR/key-repetition decoding, mandatory skip of malformed and non-UTF-8 nodes, and the exact case/hyphen/digit normalization of the secret token. Hidden generalization comes from three genuinely different relay trees (fresh set, adversarial decoy set incl. a convention-matching but non-UTF-8 node, and an edge set with hyphen/dot/long unpadded names) that the deliverable must pass via the same CLI interface. Dropped the hard-floor reverse-engineered radix/range decoder competency (C-e41d6ebb) to keep the task coherent at the medium target.

echo-mantle.notes: hard bucket (total 20). One provisioning script binds several competencies: launch & keep three JVM daemon replicas alive and serve a healthy cluster report over a TCP HTTP RPC port writing /app/status.json; repair DNS/name-resolution and hostname via persistent files; declare a mailing-list config in the canonical /etc/postfix/relay_lists and switch list mail to local delivery (transport_maps + rebuilt aliases); parse/aggregate a provided pcap into sorted 5-tuple network flows; capture the terminal ending text byte-for-byte into /app/answer.txt; persist mailreader's default login shell as /bin/bash. Verifier executes /app/setup.sh plus /app/pcap_to_netflow.py on hidden captures (incl. malformed/truncated), compares flow JSON exactly, and checks byte-identical answer text. dependent_stages=3>=2 and reasoning_depth=3>=2, meeting the hard-commitment rule.

elm-keystone.documented_probe: The 'match a reference behavior under a numeric tolerance' competency (C-8d6b9acc) has a hard floor in its reference form (onnx-style float drift on fixed+random inputs); here the numeric parity is a deterministic integer knapsack objective that must be reconstructed by the same reference algorithm on both fixed and hidden inputs and compared exactly (an error bound of 0, subsuming 'within tolerance'). That specific dimension is simpler than its reference floor, while the sibling exact-format and spreadsheet-cell competencies carry the task to medium.
elm-keystone.notes: Medium. A byte-exact artifact-pack pipeline: the agent must internally solve per-zone 0/1 knapsacks (capacity = 15 + len(zone)) with a documented lexicographic tie-break, compute an integer objective, and emit seven exact artifacts (plan_records.csv, decisions.txt, objective.txt, final_report.csv with exact column set/order, transformed/<zone>.csv files, schema-exact answer.json, and a schedule.xlsx built via the openpyxl cell API at exact addresses). quantitative_correctness=2 (optimal knapsack value + set must match the reference exactly). adversarial_inputs=2 (hidden cases mix malformed/invalid rows, duplicates, boundary slots 0/47 vs 48/-1, and optimizer-value ties that force the tie-break). hidden_case_generalization=2 (verifier re-runs solve.py on three fresh hidden inputs and diffs every artifact). reasoning_depth=2 (knapsack + tie-break + exact formats). Bucket total = 11 -> medium.

elm-ridge.notes: Medium. A reproducible provisioning pipeline: create two named venvs with a specified 3.12 interpreter, install a pinned auto-installed package plus a small package from a local offline index, upgrade a bundled data library from 1.4.0 to >= 2.0.0 to expose an absent keyword, generate gRPC bindings from a proto into the server venv and install a chain-query helper, wire a Jupyter notebook server config, and persist a requirements.lock matching the installed pins. dependent_stages=2 (venv creation -> package install -> bindings/lock; each stage feeds the next). hidden_case_generalization=2 because the verifier re-runs provision.sh from four genuinely different pre-existing filesystem states (absent, partial, stale-downgraded, corrupt) that a robust idempotent script must recover from. adversarial_inputs=1 (stale and corrupt seeds). debugging_ambiguity=1 (interpreter/locator/venv-flag mistakes only show up at runtime). Bucket total = 10 -> medium.

elm-summit.notes: Hard (19/30). The load is integration: authoring a real gRPC AtlasGateway (protobuf service, durable atomic JSON KV store, online status report), launching + keeping alive a background mlflow tracking server on 127.0.0.1:8080, and making the single deliverable generalize to undisclosed cluster configs/ports including a restart/persistence check. Success requires juggling multiple live processes, a correct gRPC round-trip on new input, and exact cluster/capacity reporting. Reasoning_depth and dependent_stages are 3, debugging_ambiguity is 2, so difficulty does not come from prompt length. Nothing is claimed below the competency floors (grpc: medium, cluster-status: easy, mlflow: easy).

elm-terrace.notes: Hard. A multi-stage (dependent_stages=3) model-artifact tuning pipeline: reconstruct a network purely from a state dict's key/shapes (reasoning_depth=3: infer in/hidden/out/blocks; handle both bare and wrapped tensor containers), fit rank-2 LoRA adapters on CPU under a 100KB serialized-model ceiling (resource_pressure=1), sample 1000 rows from the intervened model, emit one out-of-sample prediction per holdout row, produce low-rank factor matrices, and run a @triton.jit kernel through the TRITON_INTERPRET=1 CPU path. debugging_ambiguity=2: exact adapter_config fields (r=2, alpha=8, target_modules, CAUSAL_LM), Triton interpreter vs hardware, strict state-dict load errors. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden architectures vary hidden dim and block count; the verifier re-runs reconstruct.py load on hidden dicts and requires an exact parameter reproduction (hidden_case_generalization=2, quantitative_correctness=2). Difficulty converges to hard, satisfying the hard floor of every bundled slice competency.

elm-yonder.notes: Bucket total 18 (hard). Max competency floor is hard (C-85b852b). Five distinct deliverables must all succeed: link.py coalesces per-module LLVM IR into one linkable all.bc that resolves a genuine cross-module call (C-0c70052d) and carries debug metadata from a -g rebuild of the C source (C-992ec77f); elf.py parses ELF32/ELF64 header + section-header tables honoring endianness and emits an exact address->32-bit-word JSON (C-6c1e4526, C-e1e3902d); sym.py runs a symbolic engine that covers every branch both true and false with generated concrete cases (C-cb07fa86); solver.py accepts a quantifier-free bit-vector SMT-LIB proof-of-work query on stdin and returns a verdict with zero exit code (C-5c5377bf). tool_breadth spans clang/llvm-link/llvm-dis/llvm-dwarfdump, raw ELF binary parsing, an expression parser for the symbolic conditions, and z3 SMT solving. reasoning_depth is high: deriving ELF field offsets/endianness, rebuilding the C source with -g so the IR carries debug metadata, and a correct branch-covering search. hidden_case_generalization is high because the verifier also runs link.py on an unrelated IR pair and elf.py on two freshly-compiled ELF64 binaries, feeds a sat + unsat SMT query pair (an agent that hard-codes 'sat' fails the unsat case), and runs sym.py on a 3-variable/3-gate module. quantitative_correctness covers exact word decoding and JSON equality.

ember-wheel.notes: Medium: the agent must locate a single off-by-stride defect in a small C extension, rebuild it as a CPython module, and drive a data-driven harness. Exact 8-hex checksums across empty/single/boundary/duplicate vectors require genuinely repairing the fold loop rather than hardcoding the visible report; hidden inputs (empty vectors, length-2/3 vectors that lay bare which indices are folded, values near the 32-bit ceiling) force generalization. Mixing constants are fixed and documented, so the core reasoning is contained but non-trivial.

fern-engine.notes: Hard driven by dependent_stages (a multi-stage lifecycle: cache->offline reuse; train->serialize->reload-confirm->predict; rebuild; reconfigure), by reasoning_depth (reconstructing exact layer/shape/param-name architecture solely from a raw state dict, and slicing a classification head to an arbitrary label count while keeping config in sync), by tool_breadth (torch + transformers AutoModelForCausalLM/AutoTokenizer with local_files_only), and by hidden-case generalization (a different causal LM, a different state-dict shape, a different label count, unseen training data must all work via the same program). Malformed inputs (bad state file, header-only CSV, nonexistent cache, K=0, missing input) are fed and must fail cleanly, requiring defensive validation. Sanity is medium-weight data only, no GPU/resource pressure, so it caps out in the low-mid hard bucket.

fern-hearth.notes: Three independent competencies must all be met for full reward. (1) A git post-receive hook must deploy pushed branch trees to /app/deployed/<branch> (mirroring file trees byte-for-byte, updating in place, removing on branch delete, and safely ignoring non-branch refs while never writing outside the served root). (2) A URL normalizer must convert trailing-slash, query-ordering, default-port and case variants to one canonical form and stay idempotent over malformed/blank lines. (3) Each paper in the bundled index must be enumerated from the HTML and its author-maintained repository resolved by cross-referencing the affiliation org against candidate repo URLs; the mapping is validated by re-parsing all papers, including missing-detail and missing-affiliation edge cases. Reasoning depth is high because the deployed tree must exactly mirror the pushed branch trees (byte-equality), and the paper mapping must be derived from parsing + cross-referencing, not from a visible list.

fern-terrace.notes: Hard bucket (sum=21): brings up a full guest OS under software-emulated QEMU (no /dev/kvm) with a custom assembly-less initramfs, wired hostfwd networking, and leaves the emulator alive as a background service (C-3654b094, floor hard); recovers a marker from a legacy raw disk image by parsing the partition table at a non-trivial byte offset with e2fs tools (C-31e6f8e2, floor hard); and establishes password-based root SSH from the host into the running guest with a successful remote command (C-90061c28, floor medium). The same builder must generalize over hidden profiles/disks of differing offsets, hosts and tokens, so hidden_case_generalization and dependent_stages are high; TCG boot latency and sequential stage ordering drive resource_pressure/interaction_statefulness. Medium floor for C-90061c28 is satisfied; the two hard floors push the bucket to hard.

flint-anchor.notes: Hard (total 18). Five subsystems of a compiler/runtime toolchain must each be repaired and then generalize: (1) the call-site grouper keys traces by the top three innermost frames and must reproduce exact top-10 counts on hidden traces including <3-frame samples; (2) an RLE free-space GC sweep has an introduced off-by-one that must be located by reasoning about the sweep path (hard floor, debugging_ambiguity/reasoning_depth 3); (3) a template using a post-C++11 relaxed-constexpr body must be ported to strict C++11 while keeping constexpr sums exact; (4) the mkbin tool must assemble emitted IR, link it against a project shared library and produce a runnable executable validated on hidden IR/lib pairs; (5) the ELF section/symbol resolver must parse section headers and resolve names through the symbol string table exactly. The resolver runs on ELFs produced by the IR build stage, hence dependent_stages 2. Hidden generalization is exercised across all modules (hidden traces, randomized+adversarial sweep heaps, hidden static_assert packs, three hidden IR/lib cases, and extra ELF samples); correctness must be byte/line exact. All components are lean (no real compiler bootstrap, no full OS install, no hypervisor): they exercise the same competency slivers through small C/C++/ELF programs.

flint-cipher.notes: Three staged artifacts that each depend on the previous stage (vocabulary filtering -> bounded BPE -> snapshot/re-eval of a multilingual classifier), and the verifier re-runts all three builders on brand-new hidden corpora/splits. Difficulty = 19 (hard bucket). The classifier must generalize to unseen held-out documents and stay above overall and per-language accuracy floors; hidden probes include a required term whose raw frequency is below the threshold, single-occupancy filler words that must be filtered out, an empty-ish tiny corpus, and a document with no usable features.

flint-ember.documented_probe: C-f5ee7735 and C-6ce533a8 reference optimizers are deliberately simplified: the knapsack here is a tiny enumerable 0/1 instance (<=6 projects, unique optimum) rather than an integer-program of useful scale, so the 'optimize' step never needs a real solver. The exactness schema/output contract around the objective is kept in full.
flint-ember.notes: Medium. A single Python pipeline must emit five byte-exact artifacts: JSONL plan records, a decision/NPV text block, a pandas-read CSV with an exact column set/order, a salted deterministic results.json, an integer objective answer, and openpyxl cells at exact addresses. Reasoning about the knapsack optimum plus strict output-format correctness and hidden-input generalization carry the difficulty; no heavy tools, resource pressure, or safety penalties.

flint-fathom.notes: A five-stage video pipeline: (1) HTTP-fetch the mirrored source clip into /app/source.mp4 via a small local mirror server; (2) ffmpeg-trim the source to keep only the trailing 60 frames into /app/clip.mp4; (3) write a pure-CPU frame-analysis script (opencv-headless) /app/detect_frames.py that reports the exact frame where a monocular running subject leaves the ground and the frame where it returns; (4) write /app/extract_commands.py that turns a typed-command session transcript into the ordered verb-phrase commands; (5) emit /app/commands.txt (one command per line) and /app/events.json. The verifier re-executes the two real programs on freshly hidden inputs (three annotated jump clips with clean / never-returns / no-jump scenarios and an unseen transcript) and byte-checks the two emitted files. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (a working end-to-end DAG from download through trim to event detection and serialization), reasoning_depth (invent a position-tracking detection algorithm robust to a coarse baseline and null/ambiguous flight states), adversarial_inputs (hidden clips that never exhibit a takeoff or never exhibit a landing must yield explicit nulls, plus an all-grounded clip = both null, and a malformed/empty transcript), and quantitative_correctness (exact frame indices), with tool_breadth spanning ffmpeg/ffprobe, an HTTP mirror fetch, OpenCV/numpy and CSV-log parsing.

flint-mantle.notes: Multi-part deterministic contract: reverse translation, exact FASTA bytes incl. wrapping/newline, self-reported hash, constraint-satisfaction primer selection with tie-break rules, error handling. Every rule is byte-checked on hidden cases.
